hints: Focus on how violently reactive sodium metal is, especially with anything containing water or replaceable hydrogen.
Remember that sodium reacts with water to make hydrogen gas, which is highly flammable, so anything that can release hydrogen is unsafe.
Look for the one material that is completely inert and will simply cover and isolate the metal from air and moisture.
walkthrough:
**Recall how sodium behaves**

Think of sodium as a metal desperate to lose its outer electron. It reacts violently with any source of $\text{H}^+$, including water and acids, to release hydrogen gas.

$$2\text{Na} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NaOH} + \text{H}_2$$

**Check what each liquid would make**

Dilute acid reacts even more violently than water to give $\text{H}_2$. Water spray gives $\text{H}_2$ plus heat that can ignite it. Even ethanol reacts to give flammable hydrogen, just more slowly.

$$2\text{Na} + 2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} \rightarrow 2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{ONa} + \text{H}_2$$

**Choose the inert cover**

Sand, mainly $\text{SiO}_2$, does not react with sodium at all. It smothers the spillage, keeps air and moisture away, and lets you safely collect the metal without making any toxic or flammable products.

options.A: Incorrect. Dilute hydrochloric acid reacts extremely vigorously with sodium to form hydrogen gas and a lot of heat: $2\text{Na} + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow 2\text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2$. This is even more dangerous than water.
options.B: Incorrect. Ethanol does react more gently than water, but it still produces flammable hydrogen gas: $2\text{Na} + 2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} \rightarrow 2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{ONa} + \text{H}_2$. It fails the requirement of no flammable products.
options.C: Correct. Sand is inert to sodium. It covers the metal, excludes oxygen and moisture, prevents fire, and produces no toxic or flammable products, so it is the safe clean-up material.
options.D: Incorrect. Water spray reacts violently with sodium to give sodium hydroxide and flammable hydrogen gas, with enough heat to ignite the hydrogen. This is exactly what must be avoided.
